service.description: The communication events a party is from or to, or has a CommunicationEventParty row on (a to or cc recipient, a watcher, or a party the event was filed on), newest first unless ordered otherwise. Posts to a mailbox (contactListId set) belong to the mailbox's members and are left out unless includeListPosts is true, a contactListId is given, or the post was filed on the party (its _NA_ row, link#CommunicationEventRecord).

actions.script: linkedPostIds = includeListPosts || contactListId ? [] : Array.from(ec.entity.find('mantle.party.communication.CommunicationEventPartyAndEvent') .condition('partyId', partyId).condition('roleTypeId', '_NA_').condition('contactListId', 'not-equals', null) .selectField('communicationEventId').list()).map((row) => row.communicationEventId)

service.description:
A communication event, by default an internal Message from the current user's party. Each recipient gets a CommunicationEventParty row, which holds that recipient's own read, flag, archive and snooze state: the parties of toPartyId and toPartyIdList (role MessageTo), of ccPartyIdList and mentionPartyIdList (an @mention is a cc; MessageCc), and for a post to a mailbox (a contactListId of type MAILBOX) the mailbox's current members and the participants of the thread (MessageMailbox), less the poster. A party gets one row, its role by that priority: to, then cc, then mailbox. toPartyId is set to the first to-party.
A post must be allowed by the mailbox's posting policy for the from party (mantle.marketing.ContactListServices.get#ContactListAccess). A post in a thread (parentCommEventId, or rootCommEventId, which defaults to the parent's thread) must be in that mailbox's thread, and the thread must not be closed (its first post CeResolved). The participants of a thread are the parties its messages are from or to and its to and cc recipients; besides the members they get the post where they may read the thread (a public mailbox, or their own threads in a help mailbox). A contactListId of another type (Marketing's lists) is only set on the event, as before.
A Message alerts the users of the recipients that take it in the Inbox on topic NewMail (notify#NewMail: not the members who take the mailbox as Mailbox only); newMailUserIds are those alerted.

parameter.name: toPartyIdList
parameter.description: To recipients after toPartyId

parameter.name: mentionPartyIdList
parameter.description: Parties mentioned with @, added as cc

parameter.name: recipientList
parameter.description: The CommunicationEventParty rows written: {partyId, roleTypeId}

parameter.name: newMailUserIds
parameter.description: The users alerted on topic NewMail

service.description: A reply to a communication event (parentCommEventId) in its thread (rootCommEventId), through create#Message. A reply to a Message is a Message, and a reply to anything else a Comment to the parent's other party, as before (request, task and wiki comment replies). A reply to a Message is a reply all: a mailbox post's reply goes to its mailbox (create#Message adds the members and the thread's participants); any other goes to the parent's sender and its To recipients, with its Cc recipients as cc, less the replier. replyToSenderOnly answers only the parent's sender (its recipient when the replier sent it), as an internal message off the mailbox. toPartyIdList, ccPartyIdList and mentionPartyIdList add recipients. The from party must be able to see the parent Message: from, to or a recipient of it, or a post of a mailbox it may read.

For find#InternalThreads and get#InternalThread: the messages of threads (by root id) the current user's party may see, oldest first, each with that party's rows (myRowList), its to and cc recipients and its attachments; per thread its mailbox and what the party may do there. Cancelled messages are left out; a thread with no visible message is not in threadMap.

parameter.name: threadMap
parameter.description: Root id to {rootCommEventId, root, subject, contactListId, contactListName, isMailbox, isClosed, takesPart, canReadAll, canPost, canModerate, messageList}

service.description:
The current user's internal threads, a row per thread (the root message and its replies), newest first by sortDate: the date of the thread's newest message that puts it in the view.
Views: received (the default: the Inbox, threads with a to or cc row of the user's, or a mailbox row of a mailbox delivered to the Inbox, not archived and not snoozed), sent (threads with a message from the user), flagged, snoozed (snoozedThruDate in the future; those threads are out of received until then), archived (every row of the user's in the thread archived), all (any thread with a row of the user's). With contactListId, the threads of that mailbox (view all is its default; the other views then go by the user's rows on its posts): every thread for a member or a public mailbox, the user's own in a help mailbox, none for a party with only a join request; a post with no row of the user's is read. comments is the view of the internal notes (Comment, such as a Chatter note that mentions the user) with a row of the user's. unreadOnly keeps threads with an unread message for the user. needsReply keeps the threads whose last message is to the user (a to or cc row, not a mailbox delivery), not from the user, a day old or more, and not archived (Comms Home's Needs reply).
The search line: searchText, read by org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.parse#SearchText, or searchTermMap, what that service answered (find#InboxThreads parses once for both stores). A message puts its thread in the view when it matches every term; the operators mean what they mean for mail (find#Messages), over the internal fields: from: the party it is from, to: its to or cc recipients (and toPartyId), cc: its cc recipients, each a party whose name, user name or email address has the text; subject:; before:, after:, older_than: and newer_than: its date; in: the view (inbox received, sent, flagged or starred, snoozed, archive, all or anywhere). The thread's state: is:unread, is:read, is:flagged (starred), is:snoozed, has:attachment and filename: (an attachment's name). A word is in the subject or body or the sender's name, a "phrase" in the subject or body, and a -word in neither. label: is a label the user put on a message of the thread (CommunicationEventPartyLabel, an EmailLabel of the user's Internal account; the name contains the text). What internal messages do not have matches none of them, and with a - matches all: bcc:, larger: and smaller: (no size), is:answered, and an in: of a mail-only view (drafts, scheduled, outbox, spam, trash) or a folder. A date or size the operator does not understand is an error. With emailLabelId, only threads the user labeled with that label.
Paging: pageSize threads, and beforeDate, the sortDate of the last thread shown (nextBeforeDate), for the next page. A row is {store (internal), threadId and rootCommEventId (the root's id), lastCommEventId, communicationEventTypeId, subject, snippet (the last message as text), sortDate, lastDate, firstDate (epoch millis), messageCount, replyCount, unreadCount, isUnread, isFlagged, isArchived, snoozedThruDate, hasAttachment, fromPartyId (of the last message), participantPartyIdList, participantList ({partyId, name}), contactListId, contactListName, isClosed, labelList ({emailLabelId, labelName, color})}; the store and the date cursor let find#InboxThreads merge it with the framework's mail.

parameter.name: view
parameter.description: received, sent, flagged, snoozed, archived, comments or all

parameter.name: emailLabelId
parameter.description: Only threads the user labeled with this label of the Internal account

parameter.name: searchTermMap
parameter.description: The answer of parse#SearchText, in place of searchText

parameter.name: nextBeforeDate
parameter.description: The sortDate of the last row, when hasMore

service.description: The messages of a thread the current user may see, oldest first, by any message of it (communicationEventId) or its root (rootCommEventId); a message or thread the user may not see is "not found". Each message has its fields, its to and cc recipients, its attachments, and myState: the user's row {roleTypeId, readDate, isFlagged, archivedDate, snoozedThruDate}, null when the user has none (a post read through the mailbox, or a message the user sent). It marks nothing read; set#InternalMessageState does. canReply is false for a closed thread or a mailbox the user may not post to. labelList is the labels this user put on any message of the thread (CommunicationEventPartyLabel). Another party's labels are not in it. Internal messages have no folders.

parameter.name: labelList
parameter.description: Labels this user put on any message of the thread: {emailLabelId, labelName, color}

service.description: Sets the current user's state of a message (communicationEventId) or of every message of a thread (rootCommEventId): read (true sets readDate, false clears it), flagged, archived (archivedDate), and snoozedThruDate (hidden from the Inbox until then; unsnooze clears it). It updates every row the user's party has on each message. A mailbox post the user reads without a row (a member who joined later) gets a MessageMailbox row, on the message or the thread's last post, when the change is more than marking it read.

parameter.name: rootCommEventId
parameter.description: The whole thread

parameter.name: communicationEventIdList
parameter.description: The messages whose rows changed

service.description: Puts labels on, or takes them off, a message the current user may see (communicationEventId) or every visible message of a thread (rootCommEventId). Each label is an EmailLabel of the user's Internal account (org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.ensure#InternalAccount); any other is "Email label X not found". The join is CommunicationEventPartyLabel, so two people on the same message label it apart, and a reply does not inherit a label. Linking a label that is already on the message, or removing one that is not, changes nothing. A message or thread the user may not see is "not found". At least one label to add or remove.

parameter.name: rootCommEventId
parameter.description: Every visible message of the thread

parameter.name: communicationEventIdList
parameter.description: The messages whose labels changed

service.description: An owner or moderator of a mailbox closes a thread (any message of it): its first post gets status CeResolved, and the thread takes no more replies in the mailbox. reopen=true opens it again (CeReceived).

The unread internal messages delivered to a party's Inbox (the party, or the user's party; the current user's by default), each message once: its to and cc rows and its mailbox rows of mailboxes it takes in the Inbox (a member's delivery CldInbox, or a participant of a thread who is not a member), not archived and not snoozed. unreadThreadCount counts their threads. For the header's Inbox count (get#ShellCounts).

The Inbox's one list over both stores, newest first by sortDate: the framework's mail (org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.find#Messages, rows with store email) and the internal threads (find#InternalThreads, store internal). A store is called only when the view includes it.
The view: - With no emailAccountId and no contactListId: view inbox (the default: the Unified inbox, every mail account's Inbox and the internal received view), flagged, snoozed, sent, archive and all read both stores (the internal views received, flagged, snoozed, sent, archived and all); scheduled, outbox, drafts, junk and trash read only the mail, and so does emailFolderId (view folder). emailLabelId of a mail account reads only that account's mail (view label). emailLabelId of the Internal account, with no mail account named, reads only the internal threads. - emailAccountId of a mail account: that account's mail only, in view (inbox by default), its folder (emailFolderId) or its label (emailLabelId). A label of the Internal account is not that account's. - emailAccountId of the user's Internal account, or store internal: the internal threads only, in view received (or inbox, the default), sent, flagged, snoozed, archived (or archive) or all. A label (emailLabelId) is allowed; a view with no internal counterpart, such as label, is read as all. A folder is refused. A view with no internal counterpart and no label (drafts) lists nothing. - contactListId: the threads of that mailbox only (view all by default, else an internal view). - store email keeps the mail of a view that reads both stores; view comments (the internal notes to the user) reads only the internal threads. Filters: searchText, the search line, is read once by org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.parse#SearchText: the mail gets the text (find#Messages applies its operators) and the internal threads its terms (find#InternalThreads says what each operator means there), so both stores answer the same search; termList is the operators, for the query chips. A term that is not understood (before:someday, larger:huge) is an error before any store is read. An in: of a view that has an internal counterpart (inbox, sent, flagged, snoozed, archive, all) is the internal view too; one of a mail-only view (drafts, scheduled, outbox, spam, trash) or a folder reads only the mail. unreadOnly and needsReply (the threads waiting for the user's answer a day or more: Comms Home's Needs reply; for mail, the newest message in the view not answered and no message sent in the thread after it) go to both stores. fromAddress, toAddress, subject, hasAttachment, fromDate, thruDate, minSize and maxSize (the fields of a mail search form) are the mail's only; with any of them the internal store is not read. threadMode false lists the mail by message; internal rows are always threads.
Paging: pageSize rows (default 50), then cursor, the nextCursor of the page before. The cursor holds each store's own date cursor, store:millis (the sortDate of the last row of that store shown) or store:end (no more rows), joined by commas; a store not in it starts at its newest row. Each page reads pageSize + 1 rows of every store still going (from its own date), merges them by sortDate (mail first on the same date), keeps the first pageSize and moves each store's date to its last row kept, so a store whose rows were all newer or all older than the other's continues exactly where it stopped. A store's date is exclusive (its next page reads rows before it), so a page never ends inside a run of one store's rows with the same sortDate: that run, and the rows of the other store older than it, wait for the next page; only a run longer than a page is cut (logged). hasMore is true while a store that answered has more rows; nextCursor is empty when it is false.
Failure tolerant: each store reads in a transaction of its own; one that fails is logged, named in failedStores, and keeps its date in nextCursor, so a later page tries it again; the other store's rows still come. Strict on access: an emailAccountId, emailFolderId or emailLabelId the user does not reach, or a mailbox the user may not see, is an error before any store is read, and each store reads only what the user may read. The rows are the stores' own (find#Messages and find#InternalThreads describe them), with rowKey added: store:threadId (email:emailMessageId for the mail listed by message).

parameter.name: store
parameter.description: email or internal: only that store

parameter.name: storeList
parameter.description: The stores the view reads: email, internal

parameter.name: termList
parameter.description: The operators of searchText, each {operator, value, negate}

service.description: The unread counts of the Inbox rail and Comms Home for the current user, each part on its own: accountList, the user's accounts as org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.get#UserEmailAccounts gives them (the Internal account first; each mail account with its Inbox unreadCount and its folders' counts), with the Internal account's unreadCount filled from count#UnreadInternalMessages (internal messages and the mailbox posts delivered to the Inbox); mailboxList, the mailboxes the user is a member of or asked to join with their unreadCount and the user's delivery (mantle.marketing.ContactListServices.find#ContactLists); emailUnreadCount (the mail accounts' Inbox unread), internalUnreadCount and unifiedUnreadCount (both: the Unified inbox). A part that fails is logged by name, named in failedParts, and its counts are null.

An alert on topic NewMail for new mail in an Inbox. The topic is not persisted (persistOnSend N), so the Notifications and Updates lists and their counts leave it out; the Inbox and its count keep the message. - An email (emailMessageId): to the users of its account (the owner and the current members), when it is received mail (ES_RECEIVED) in an Inbox folder, unread, not archived and not snoozed. Coalesced by the messages themselves: mail stored in the account's Inbox within coalesceSeconds (15 by default; 0 for none) of each other alerts once, for the first stored (lastUpdatedStamp, then emailMessageId), with newCount the unread messages of that burst; for the others the users are named in coalescedUserIds. So a sync batch, one transaction or several close together, alerts once. - An internal message or mailbox post (communicationEventId, a Message): to the users of its recipients that take it in the Inbox (its to and cc rows, and its mailbox rows but those of a member who takes the mailbox as Mailbox only), less the sender. Not coalesced unless coalesceSeconds is given. The message has store, emailMessageId or communicationEventId, threadId, emailAccountId, contactListId and contactListName, fromName, fromAddress, subject and summary; the notification's record is the message and its actor the sender's user. Never fails the caller: a failure is logged and notifies no one.

parameter.name: coalesceSeconds
parameter.description: For email: 15 by default, 0 for no coalescing

parameter.name: newCount
parameter.description: The messages the alert is for

service-call.name: create#mantle.party.communication.CommunicationEvent

service.description: Mantle's rows that name a wiki page, removed before org.moqui.impl.WikiServices.delete#WikiPage deletes the page (the SECA WikiPageDeleteJoins), which would otherwise fail on their foreign keys: its comments' WikiPageCommunicationEvent joins (the comments themselves stay), its WikiPageWorkEffort and WikiPageRequest joins, and its followers (RecordFollower). The page is wikiPageId, or wikiSpaceId and pagePath as the delete finds it (get#WikiPageId, an alias of a moved page included). Only for a user who may update the page (get#WikiPageAccess); the delete refuses anyone else, and a refused delete is an error that rolls this back.

actions.script: let pageId = wikiPageId || null if (!pageId && wikiSpaceId && pagePath) pageId = ec.service.sync().name('org.moqui.impl.WikiServices.get#WikiPageId') .parameters({wikiSpaceId: wikiSpaceId, pagePath: pagePath}).call()?.wikiPageId || null if (!pageId) return const access = ec.service.sync().name('org.moqui.impl.WikiServices.get#WikiPageAccess').parameter('wikiPageId', pageId).call() if (!access?.canUpdate) return for (const entityName of ['mantle.party.communication.WikiPageCommunicationEvent', 'mantle.work.effort.WikiPageWorkEffort', 'mantle.request.WikiPageRequest']) ec.entity.find(entityName).condition('wikiPageId', pageId).disableAuthz().deleteAll() ec.entity.find('mantle.party.communication.RecordFollower').condition({recordEntityName: 'moqui.resource.wiki.WikiPage', recordId: pageId}).disableAuthz().deleteAll()

service.description: Which records a client contact who signs in sees (design-projects.md §1.1, §15 Client access and Chatter for client users; impl-projects.md P10), for userId (the current user when empty), by mantle.work.ProjectServices get#ClientProjectInfo; isClient false (and nothing visible) for a user who is not one: - a work effort: a client project; a work item (WetTask) of one shared with the client (visibility All users or General); a milestone or release of one. No other kind (sprints, events, activities). - a request: one the user filed; or of a client project, filed by one of the user's organization's contacts (clientContactPartyIds) or with one of those or the organization as a current RequestParty. - a communication event: never a Comment (a note is internal); a status update posted for the client (statusUpdateIds); a message the user's party is from, to or a party to; a message one of the organization's contacts or the organization is from, to or a party to that is filed (the event, or the root of its thread, by its own join or a CommunicationEventRecord) on a work effort or request the user sees by the rules above. Strict: a failure is an error, so a caller deciding access refuses. Every read is with authorization disabled, so the answer does not depend on the caller's filters.

What the record link and timeline services know about a record type: the full entity name and its single primary key field, the record's own communication event join, work effort join and request join (null when the generic CommunicationEventRecord, WorkEffortRecord or RequestRecord holds its links; a party's own communication event link is the event's from and to party and its CommunicationEventParty rows), its note entity and its content entity.
With checkRecord (the default) the record must be one the user may see, or there is an error (the record is not found). With checkOnly the answer is recordVisible, true or false, and no error, so the caller's transaction is not marked rollback-only by a record the user may not see; notVisibleReason says why, for a log.
A record the user may see is found under the user's entity filters, and is never someone else's personal contact (Party.privateOwnerUserId). A work effort, a request, a communication event and an order (whose filter is on OrderPart, not OrderHeader) have no entity filter of their own, so under an organization filter they follow per-user rules, those of search#Universal (IronStone R4, R5). The organization filter is the MANTLE_USER_ORG or MANTLE_ACTIVE_ORG filter set of the authorization: its organizations are filterOrgIds (setup#UserOrganizationInfo), the active organization for MANTLE_ACTIVE_ORG, and all of the user's organizations when the authorization names MANTLE_ACTIVE_ORG and no organization is active (the set's applyCond leaves it off then, but the user still has the filter here). - A work effort (task, event, project, ...): its ownerPartyId, or that of its root work effort, is the user's party or one of the user's organizations, or one of those is a current WorkEffortParty of it or of its root work effort; or it is in a calendar (CalendarWorkEffort, the series' for an instance changed on its own) the user may view (mantle.work.CalendarServices.check#CalendarAccess: view, edit or manage, not free/busy only), or it is visible to all users (visibilityEnumId WevAllUsers), as check#EventAccess has it. - A request: the user's party filed it (filedByPartyId), or the user's party or one of the user's organizations (such as the customer organization) is a current RequestParty, or the organization of its product store or the owner of its facility is one of the user's organizations, or (IronStone Projects, design-projects.md §1.1) the user sees its project (rootWorkEffortId, by ProjectServices.get#VisibleProjectInfo), or it has no project and is of a type the Projects intake of one of the user's organizations triages (a ProjIntake PartySetting of the organization; RequestServices.get#IntakeSettings triagedTypes). - An order: the user's party entered it (enteredByPartyId), or the user's party or one of the user's organizations is the vendor or customer of one of its parts (the rule of the OrderPart filter) or an OrderPartParty of it. - A communication event: the user's party is its from or to party or a CommunicationEventParty, or it is a post of a mailbox the user may read (ContactListServices.get#UserMailboxAccess), or it or the root of its thread is linked (the record's own join or a CommunicationEventRecord) to a record the user may see by these rules, one level deep: a linked communication event is checked without its own links. A post of a mailbox the user may not read follows the communication event rule with or without an organization filter, as in search#Universal, and so does a communication event filed on a wiki page the user may not see (the event or the root of its thread, WikiPageCommunicationEvent). Without an organization filter work efforts, requests, orders and other communication events are seen as found. A wiki page has its own rule (below). Any other record type has only its entity filters.
A client contact (the PROJECT_CLIENT permission) sees only what get#ClientRecordVisibility shows it, with authorization disabled too.
The per-user rules do not apply with authorization disabled (an internal caller), to a user in the ADMIN group, or for a record type the user has an explicit entity authorization for: an ArtifactAuthz of one of the user's groups over an ArtifactGroupMember of type AT_ENTITY naming the record entity (by name, or by a pattern that matches it), allow or always, for view or all, with no deny, which ec.artifactExecution.isPermitted confirms. A staff app such as a customer service or projects app gives its users all requests or work efforts that way. isPermitted alone does not tell: an entity inherits the authorization of the app root (an AUTHZT_ALWAYS ArtifactAuthz with inheritAuthz), which permits every entity to every user of the app, and no group, ADMIN included, has an entity authorization by default.
A wiki page (moqui.resource.wiki.WikiPage, a framework entity, which no entity filter covers) follows the wiki's own view rule whenever authorization is on, for every user, staff included as in the wiki screens, with or without an organization filter: org.moqui.impl.WikiServices.get#WikiPageAccess, its canView. A space with restrictView Y needs a WikiSpaceUser row of the user with allowView or allowAdmin Y, and a page with restrictView Y a WikiPageUser row of the user with allowView Y; the ADMIN group sees every page; a page whose space is not found is not seen.
A merge request or a git repository (moqui.resource.GitMergeRequest, GitRepository, framework entities no entity filter covers) is seen by whoever may view the repository (org.moqui.impl.GitServices.get#GitRepositoryAccess, canView), whenever authorization is on, as a wiki page is; so are the review comments filed on a merge request.
A timesheet (mantle.work.time.Timesheet, which no entity filter covers) is seen by its person, its approvers and ADMIN (mantle.work.TimesheetServices.get#TimesheetAccess, canView) whenever authorization is on.

parameter.description: The full entity name

service.description: The CommunicationEvent of a framework EmailMessage (by emailMessageId), created when there is none (create#EmailCommunicationEvent: type Email, its parties matched by user account and by the email addresses on parties, the status from the message's, and the parent event of the message's parent email when it has one). A message of a mail client account (emailAccountId) is found only by a user who reaches the account (org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.get#EmailAccountAccess); the personal contacts that match are the account owner's and the current user's. Mail with no account (template mail, the old poller) is found by anyone, as before.

Internal (authorization disabled), for findOrCreate#EmailCommunicationEvent and the filing of received and sent mail (file#ReceivedEmail, file#SentEmail): the CommunicationEvent of a framework EmailMessage, the one it has or a new one. Its parties are matched by the message's user accounts (fromUserId, toUserId) and by the email addresses on parties (an email address of PartyContactMechInfo in effect, in any case) for the from address and each To and Cc address. A disabled party does not match, nor a personal contact (Party.privateOwnerUserId) of a user not in contactOwnerUserIdList; a directory party comes before a personal contact of the same address.
The new event is type Email, from the from party, to the first matched To party, with the status from the message's (ES_SENT CeSent, ES_RECEIVED CeReceived, ...), the parent event of the message's parent email, and its subject and body. Every other matched To and Cc party gets a CommunicationEventParty row (MessageTo, MessageCc; one per party, To first), so each party's timeline (find#PartyCommunicationEvents) shows the email. With requireMatch nothing is created unless an address that is not in ignoreAddressList (the account's own addresses) matches a party; communicationEventId is then null.

parameter.name: contactOwnerUserIdList
parameter.description: The users whose personal contacts may match

parameter.name: ignoreAddressList
parameter.description: Addresses whose match alone does not make an event

service.description: Files a communication event on a record. The link is the record's own join when it has one (OrderCommunicationEvent, RequestCommEvent, WorkEffortCommEvent, WikiPageCommunicationEvent). For a party it is the event's from or to party, or the party's CommunicationEventParty row, written with role _NA_ (Not Applicable: a party the event is about, not a recipient) when the party has none; for a mailbox post (contactListId), which stays off the party timelines of its members and participants, it is always the _NA_ row. Any other record gets a CommunicationEventRecord. Linking again changes nothing. The event is communicationEventId, or the event of a framework email (emailMessageId), created when there is none. With notifyFollowers a new link notifies the record's followers of messages (of notes for a Comment). The record must be one the user sees (get#RecordLinkInfo); an internal caller (authorization disabled) that checked it before, as file#SentEmail for the records send#EmailDraft checked, passes checkRecord false.

parameter.name: recordUrl
parameter.description: The record's screen, for the follower notification's link

parameter.name: checkRecord
parameter.description: false only with authorization disabled

parameter.name: linkEntityName
parameter.description: The entity holding the link

parameter.name: created
parameter.description: True when this call wrote the link

service.description: Removes a communication event from a record: the own join row, the CommunicationEventRecord, or for a party the _NA_ CommunicationEventParty row. A party the event is from or to, or a recipient of, stays linked.

parameter.name: unlinked
parameter.description: True when a link row was removed

service.description:
Sends a mail client draft through org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.send#Draft, with the same parameters (now, at scheduledSendDate, or after the undo-send hold of holdSeconds) and the same results, and files it on records once it is sent (IronStone R6): recordEntityName and recordId, or recordList ({recordEntityName, recordId}) for several. Each record must be one the user sees (get#RecordLinkInfo) and the draft one the user may send from, or nothing changes.
The records are kept with the draft as EmailMessageRecord rows, which replace the ones it had; with none given the draft keeps the ones it has. Once the message is ES_SENT, file#SentEmail files it on each through link#CommunicationEventRecord with the emailMessageId (which makes its CommunicationEvent of type Email, with the parties its addresses match) and deletes the row. It runs from the EmailMessage ECA after the commit of the change that sent the message, whether the send went now (this call) or later (send#DueDrafts for a scheduled or held send, a retry from the Outbox), on a service worker in a transaction of its own: a filing failure can never roll back a send that went out. A message that waits (scheduled, held, or failed and in the Outbox) keeps its records, and cancel#ScheduledSend takes it back to Drafts with them. pendingRecordList is the records kept for the message: filed once the commit is done when sent is true.

parameter.name: recordUrl
parameter.description: The record's screen, for the follower notification's link

parameter.name: pendingRecordList
parameter.description: The records kept for the message: {recordEntityName, recordId}

service.description: Files a sent mail client message (ES_SENT): on the records kept for it (EmailMessageRecord, written by send#EmailDraft), through link#CommunicationEventRecord, deleting each row it files; and for an account that files every party match (recordFilingEnumId ErfAllMatches; by kind when empty: hosted and shared accounts) also with no record, when a recipient other than the account's own addresses matches a party, so the party's timeline shows the reply. The CommunicationEvent is create#EmailCommunicationEvent's; the personal contacts that match are those of the account's owner and of the users who chose the records. The EmailMessage ECA runs it after the commit of any change to ES_SENT (a send that went now, send#DueDrafts, a retry). Safe for any caller: it does only what the account's policy and the kept records say, and a message not sent yet keeps its records. Serialized per message by a lock on the message, so two runs do not both file. Failure tolerant per record: one that fails is logged, named in failedRecordList and kept.

Files a received mail client message by its account's policy and alerts its users. The EmailMessage ECA runs it after the commit of the write that stored the message (created ES_RECEIVED or ES_VIEWED in an account), so it never fails or slows that write. Mail in a Drafts, Sent, Junk or Trash folder is not filed.
An account that files every party match (recordFilingEnumId ErfAllMatches; by kind when empty: hosted and shared business accounts) gets the message's CommunicationEvent (type Email, emailMessageId; create#EmailCommunicationEvent) when its sender or a recipient, other than the account's own addresses, matches a party with that email address, so the party's timeline and the 360s show it; the personal contacts (Party.privateOwnerUserId) that match are only the account owner's. An account that files only what is linked (ErfLinkedOnly; an external account such as a personal Gmail) files nothing here: its owner links what belongs on a record (link#CommunicationEventRecord). Received mail in an Inbox, unread, alerts the account's users on topic NewMail (notify#NewMail, coalesced per user). Safe for any caller: it does only what the account's policy says. Never fails: each step that fails is logged and named in failedSteps.

parameter.name: created
parameter.description: True when this run made the CommunicationEvent

service.description: For the EmailMessage ECA (EmailMessage.eecas.xml): a received message stored in a mail client account (created ES_RECEIVED or ES_VIEWED) runs file#ReceivedEmail, and a message of an account that becomes sent (created ES_SENT or changed to it) runs file#SentEmail, each after the commit of the write on a service worker, in a transaction of its own, so filing and alerts never fail or slow the write (with no transaction in place, at once, in a new one). The EmailMessageRecord rows of a deleted message go. Never fails the write: a failure is logged.

parameter.name: serviceName
parameter.description: The filing service run or registered for the commit

service.description:
The history of a record, newest first: its communication events (messages; a Comment is a note) through the own join or CommunicationEventRecord with the replies in their threads, and for a party those it is from, to or a party to (find#PartyCommunicationEvents, mailbox posts left out unless includeListPosts); its *Note rows as notes (PartyNote, WorkEffortNote, RequestNote, OrderNote, FacilityNote); its done activities (work efforts with the purpose WepPhoneCall, WepEmail, WepToDo or WepMeeting through RequestWorkEffort, WikiPageWorkEffort or WorkEffortRecord); its changes from the entity audit log; its files (the *Content rows); and the messages of the chat room bound to it (org.moqui.impl.ChatServices.get#Timeline by the record: none when there is no room or the user may not read it). The open activities come apart in plannedActivities, soonest due first, with the assignee.
kinds limits the entries to messages, notes, activities, changes, files and chat (a list or comma-separated text; empty is all; messages includes chat). Page with pageIndex and pageSize, or by a cursor: beforeDate with seenKeys, which are nextBeforeDate and nextSeenKeys of the page before, gives the entries before that date and those of that date not shown yet, so the pages neither skip nor repeat an entry when entries share a date. beforeDate alone gives the entries strictly before it, as before seenKeys (an entry of the same date as the last one shown is not on the next page).
Each source stands alone: one that fails is logged by name and left out, and its name is in failedSources. The services of the ServiceRegister rows of type RecordTimelineSource are sources too: each gets recordEntityName, recordId, kinds (the wanted entry kinds), beforeDate and limit, and returns entryList; an entry of a registered source may have an entryKey (or an id) that is stable for it.
An entry is {kind (message, note, activity, change or file), date, entryKey (the source and the entry's key, stable for the entry: the cursor's seenKeys), authorPartyId, authorUserId, title, body, contentType, statusId, source (the entity or service it came from)} with the fields of its kind: communicationEventId, communicationEventTypeId, fromPartyId, toPartyId, parentCommEventId, rootCommEventId, emailMessageId, contactListId, editedDate (when its author last changed its text, update#RecordNote) and attachments (the CommunicationEventContent rows) for a message or a Comment note; noteDate and internalNote for a *Note row; workEffortId and purposeEnumId for an activity; auditHistorySeqId, fieldName, oldValue, newValue, oldValueDescription and newValueDescription (status descriptions) and changeReason for a change; contentKey, contentLocation and contentTypeEnumId for a file; for a chat message (kind chat, source moqui.chat.ChatEvent: the room's messages of the main timeline, not removed, edits applied) chatRoomId, eventSeq, roomName (also the title), authorName, bodyText (the body is the message's HTML), edited, threadReplyCount, chatAttachments and records (as get#Timeline has them), and url, the room at the message when chatRoomUrl is given.

parameter.name: kinds
parameter.description: A list or comma-separated: messages, notes, activities, changes, files

parameter.name: seenKeys
parameter.description: With beforeDate: the entryKey of each entry shown whose date is beforeDate (nextSeenKeys); the other entries of that date come too. A list or comma-separated.

parameter.name: chatRoomUrl
parameter.description: The app's chat screen (such as /qapps/Comms/Chat): a chat entry's url is it with chatRoomId and eventSeq

parameter.name: nextBeforeDate
parameter.description: The cursor of the next page: the date of the last entry of this one (null when it has none)

parameter.name: nextSeenKeys
parameter.description: The cursor's seenKeys: the entryKey of each entry shown so far whose date is nextBeforeDate

service.description: Chatter's Log note: a Comment communication event from the user (create#Message), filed on the record (link#CommunicationEventRecord). The users mentioned are notified on topic ChatterMention, and the record's followers of notes on topic RecordFollow, leaving out the author and those mentioned. A failed notification is logged; the note stays.

parameter.name: parentCommEventId
parameter.description: The note or message this answers

parameter.name: recordUrl
parameter.description: The record's screen, for the notifications' link

service.description: Whether the current user may change (action update) or delete (action delete) a note on a record's timeline: a Comment communication event (a note, a comment or a reply to one, not cancelled; a Message or an email once sent stays as it is) on a record the user may see (get#RecordLinkInfo with checkRecord: the entity filters and the per-user rules of IronStone R5 and R28). The note is on the record through the record's own join or a CommunicationEventRecord, of the note or of the root of its thread; for a party the note is from or to it or has a CommunicationEventParty row of it. Its author (the from party is the user's party) changes it; its author or a user in the ADMIN group deletes it, and not while it has replies. An error otherwise; a note that is not on the record is not found.

parameter.name: action
parameter.description: update or delete

parameter.name: recordEntityName
parameter.description: The full entity name

parameter.name: ownJoin
parameter.description: {entityName, keyField} when the note itself has the record's own join row (RequestCommEvent for a request); null when it is on the record otherwise

service.description: Chatter's edit of a note: its author changes the text, and the subject when given, of a note or comment on a record (check#RecordNoteAccess, action update), and editedDate is set, which the timeline shows as edited. A note on a request through its own join is changed by mantle.request.RequestServices.update#RequestComment, any other by the communication event's update. Only the users mentioned now who were not mentioned before are notified, on topic ChatterMention (notify#RecordMention): a mention in the old body is a data-mention-id of its rich text (a userId, or a partyId whose users count). The record's followers are not told again.

parameter.name: subject
parameter.description: Empty keeps the subject

parameter.name: contentType
parameter.description: Empty keeps the content type

parameter.name: mentionUserIds
parameter.description: The users the new body mentions

parameter.name: mentionPartyIds
parameter.description: The parties the new body mentions, whose users count

parameter.name: recordUrl
parameter.description: The record's screen, for the notifications' link

parameter.name: mentionedUserIds
parameter.description: The users notified: mentioned now and not before

service.description: Chatter's delete of a note: its author, or a user in the ADMIN group, deletes a note or comment on a record that has no replies (check#RecordNoteAccess, action delete). A note on a request through its own join is deleted by mantle.request.RequestServices.delete#RequestComment, any other by delete#CommunicationEventRows: the note, its links to records, its party, purpose and product rows and its attachments (their files too).

Deletes a communication event with the rows that name it: its links to records (CommunicationEventRecord, RequestCommEvent, WorkEffortCommEvent, OrderCommunicationEvent, WikiPageCommunicationEvent), its CommunicationEventParty, CommunicationEventPurpose and CommunicationEventProduct rows, and its CommunicationEventContent rows with their files under the event's content folder (a file that cannot be deleted is logged; its row is gone). An event with replies is not deleted. For the callers that checked who may delete it (delete#RecordNote, mantle.request.RequestServices.delete#RequestComment).

The users of userIds who may be told of a record's entry (impl-projects.md P10): every user who is not a client contact (the PROJECT_CLIENT permission), and a client contact only for a communication event that is for it (get#ClientRecordVisibility); without a communicationEventId (a note's activity, a change) no client contact. Strict: a client whose check fails is left out, and logged.

Notifies the users mentioned in a note or message on a record, on topic ChatterMention: mentionUserIds and the users of mentionPartyIds, less the author. The message has recordEntityName, recordId, recordName, communicationEventId, authorUserId, authorName, subject and summary; the link is recordUrl, since the record's screen belongs to the app. A failed send is logged and notifies no one.

Notifies the followers of a record whose RecordFollower row has the kind on (notifyMessages, notifyNotes, notifyActivities, notifyChanges), on topic RecordFollow, less the author and excludeUserIds. The message is that of notify#RecordMention plus kind and workEffortId. A failed send is logged and notifies no one.

parameter.name: kind
parameter.description: messages, notes, activities or changes

service.description: The message of a mention or follower notification: the record, its name in words with its id, the author's name, the subject, and a summary (the subject, or the start of the body as text).

The user (by default the current one) follows a record. kinds (a list or comma-separated: messages, notes, activities, changes) sets which notify, the others off; without it a new follower gets messages, notes and activities, and an existing one keeps its kinds. Following again updates the kinds.
The followers of a record, each with the user's name and party and which kinds notify; isFollowing for the current user.

A chat message as a communication event, made once per message: type Chat, from the sender's party, its date the message's, the room's name as its subject and the message's HTML (its last edit) as its body. The user must be able to read the room (org.moqui.impl.ChatServices.get#RoomAccess), and the message is one of the room's messages that is not removed. The event names its message by a CommunicationEventRecord of moqui.chat.ChatEvent whose recordId is chatRoomId::eventSeq (the key of the MoquiChatEvent document): it finds the event again, and is no record a timeline or the record visibility rules read. Filing it on a record is link#CommunicationEventRecord (create#RecordFromChatMessage does it for the record it makes). created is true when this call made the event; chatMessage is the message: {chatRoomId, eventSeq, senderUserId, senderName, senderPartyId, sentDate, body, bodyText, attachmentNames, roomName, roomRecordEntityName, roomRecordId}.

A task, request or event made from a chat message (the Chat message actions, IronStone design §13): recordKind task (mantle.work.TaskServices.create#SimpleTask, owned by the user and assigned to assignToPartyId, the user by default), request (mantle.request.RequestServices.create#Request, filed by the user and submitted) or event (mantle.work.EventServices.create#Event in calendarId, the user's default calendar by default, from estimatedStartDate to estimatedCompletionDate, or on allDayStart to allDayEnd; with neither, the next whole hour for an hour). Its name is name, by default the message's first line (at most 100 characters; the file names, or "Message from" the sender, for a message without text), and its description description, by default the message's text. The message becomes a communication event (findOrCreate#ChatCommunicationEvent) filed on the new record (its own join, WorkEffortCommEvent or RequestCommEvent), so the record's timeline shows where it came from. When the room is bound to a record, the new record is linked to it as well unless linkRoomRecord is false: a task or event by link#WorkEffortRecord (the record's own join, such as RequestWorkEffort, else WorkEffortRecord), a request to a work effort by RequestWorkEffort; a request has no link to another kind of record (roomRecordLinked false). A failure of that link is logged and leaves roomRecordLinked false; the rest stands.

parameter.name: recordKind
parameter.description: task, request or event

parameter.name: purposeEnumId
parameter.description: A task's (default WepTask) or an event's (default WepMeeting)

parameter.name: estimatedCompletionDate
parameter.description: A task's due date, an event's end
